t:
(a) 
The Federal Credit Union Act is amended—

        (1) in section 107(5)(A)(i)—

            (A) 
by inserting “, including an individual cooperative unit,” immediately following “dwelling”; and
 
            (B) 
by inserting “(except that a loan on an individual cooperative unit shall be adequately secured as defined by the Board)” after “thirty years”;
  
        (2) by striking out section 305(b)(3) and inserting in lieu thereof the following:



“(3) 
shall share in dividend distributions at rates determined by the Board. However, rates on the required capital stock shall be without preference; and”;



 
        (3) 
by striking out “, to the extent or in such amounts as are provided in advance in appropriation Acts” in section 307(15); and
 
        (4) 
in title III, as so redesignated by subsection (b)(1), by striking out “Administrator” each place it appears and inserting in lieu thereof “Board”.
  
    (b) 
The Federal Credit Union Act is amended—

        (1) 
by striking out the heading of subchapter III of such Act and inserting in lieu thereof “TITLE III—CENTRAL LIQUIDITY FACILITY”;
 
        (2) 
in title III, as so redesignated by paragraph (1), by striking out “subchapter” each place it appears therein and inserting in lieu thereof “title”; and
 
        (3) 
in section 307(3), by striking out “subchapters I and II of this chapter” and inserting in lieu thereof “titles I and II of this Act”.

fable.w: The section makes technical amendments to the Federal Credit Union Act and lets the Board define adequate security and set dividend rates. The tempting reading is that "as defined by the Board" implies rulemaking with public comment, but the text does not require a regulation, comment period, hearing, or consultation with any outside party. The only actor is the Board, a federal agency, so nothing crosses the federal boundary.
fable.s: (except that a loan on an individual cooperative unit shall be adequately secured as defined by the Board)

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to the Federal Credit Union Act, such as inserting definitions, changing titles, and replacing terms like 'Administrator' with 'Board'. It does not establish any process for consulting with or coordinating with outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before a federal decision is made. The mention of the 'Board' refers to the National Credit Union Board, a federal entity, and the changes are legislative edits rather than procedural requirements for public participation.
qwen_block.s: The Federal Credit Union Act is amended— (1) in section 107(5)(A)(i)— (A) by inserting “, including an individual cooperative unit,” immediately following “dwelling”; and (B) by inserting “(except that a loan on an individual cooperative unit shall be adequately secured as defined by the Board)” after “thirty years”; (2) by striking out section 305(b)(3) and inserting in lieu thereof the following: “(3) shall share in dividend distributions at rates determined by the Board. However, rates on the required capital stock shall be without preference; and”; (3) by striking out “, to the extent or in such amounts as are provided in advance in appropriation Acts” in section 307(15); and (4) in title III, as so redesignated by subsection (b)(1), by striking out “Administrator” each place it appears and inserting in lieu thereof “Board”.

opus.w: These are technical amendments to the Federal Credit Union Act: they change wording, strike an appropriations limit, and leave definitions and dividend rates to the Board. The Board is a federal agency acting on its own, and no comment period, hearing, outside advisory body, consultation with non-federal parties, or right to sue is created. One could read "as defined by the Board" as rulemaking authority, but unlike the explicit "by regulation" grant in Example 6, nothing here requires or authorizes a rulemaking.
opus.s: (except that a loan on an individual cooperative unit shall be adequately secured as defined by the Board)
opus.b: Tempting reading: "adequately secured as defined by the Board" could look like rulemaking authority, like Example 6's "may by regulation." That reading fails because the section never mentions regulations or rulemaking, and no outside party is brought into any decision. The NCUA Board is a federal agency, so the participation test is not met.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the Federal Credit Union Act to change terminology and internal agency procedures. The 'Board' mentioned is the National Credit Union Administration Board, a federal agency. There is no requirement for consultation with or participation by non-federal entities (such as the public, states, or private organizations) in the decision-making process described. The interactions are strictly within the federal government or between the federal agency and regulated entities in a regulatory/administrative capacity.
qwen_chat.s: by striking out “Administrator” each place it appears and inserting in lieu thereof “Board”
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: The text mentions a "Board" which might be an advisory body involving outside experts.
Resolution: The "Board" referred to is the National Credit Union Administration Board, which is a federal agency. The section describes amendments to the Federal Credit Union Act regarding internal agency procedures, dividend rates, and terminology. There is no requirement for consultation with or participation by non-federal entities (such as the public, states, or private organizations) in the decision-making process described. The interactions are strictly within the federal government or between the federal agency and regulated entities in a regulatory/administrative capacity (not participatory in the sense of the definition).
